module_title: Real-World Case Studies 5: Gaming, IoT & FinTech
description: End-to-end interview blueprints: Design Real-Time Gaming Leaderboard (Redis Sorted Sets), IoT Sensor Ingestion Pipeline (Kafka + Time-Series DB), and Distributed Crypto/Stock Exchange Order Book.

topics.title: Case Study: Design Real-Time Gaming Leaderboard (Redis Sorted Sets)
topics.definition: Design a real-time gaming leaderboard system for 50 million active players supporting instant score updates and sub-10ms queries for Top-100 global players and Player Rank lookups.
topics.why_we_need_it: Relational queries like `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM scores WHERE score > my_score` take 10+ seconds on 50 million rows. Redis Sorted Sets (Skip Lists) evaluate rank in $O(\log N)$ time (~1 millisecond).
topics.real_world_analogy: A physical race track scoreboard: when a car crosses the finish line, the scoreboard instantly moves their number card up the board without recalculating the times of all 10,000 cars from scratch.
topics.how_it_works:
1. Redis Sorted Sets (ZSET): Combines a Hash Map (for $O(1)$ player score lookups) with a Skip List (for $O(\log N)$ score insertion and rank retrieval).
2. Score Update: `ZINCRBY leaderboard:global 50 user_123` ($O(\log N)$).
3. Top 100 Players: `ZREVRANGE leaderboard:global 0 99 WITHSCORES` ($O(\log N + M)$ - sub-1ms).
4. Get My Rank: `ZREVRANK leaderboard:global user_123` ($O(\log N)$).
5. Time-Bounded Leaderboards: Separate Redis keys for `leaderboard:daily:2026-10-03`, `leaderboard:weekly`, and `leaderboard:monthly`.
conceptual_breakdown: Skip List Internals: Multi-level linked list with probabilistic forward pointers enabling logarithmic $O(\log N)$ search and insertion.
Tie-Breaking: When two players have identical scores, encode the earlier timestamp into the fractional part: `Final_Score = Score + (1 - (Timestamp / 1e12))` so earlier players rank higher.

topics.title: Case Study: Design IoT Telemetry Pipeline (MQTT, Kafka & TimescaleDB)
topics.definition: Design a connected-vehicle telemetry pipeline ingesting 1 million IoT smart meters / cars emitting sensor telemetry every 5 seconds (200,000 events/sec), processing alerts in real-time, and archiving for historical analytics.
topics.why_we_need_it: Tests lightweight binary protocols (MQTT), high-throughput ingest pipelines, downsampling rollups, and Time-Series Databases (TimescaleDB / InfluxDB).
topics.real_world_analogy: A network of 1 million weather stations: each station transmits temperature and humidity every 5 seconds over radio. A central weather computer alerts for forest fire heat spikes in 1 second while storing daily averages for climate research.
topics.how_it_works:
1. MQTT Ingestion: Devices connect to MQTT Brokers (EMQX / Mosquitto) over lightweight binary TCP packets.
2. Kafka Stream Buffer: MQTT broker bridges messages into Apache Kafka `sensor-telemetry` topic.
3. Real-Time Anomaly Engine: Apache Flink processes sliding windows (e.g. engine temperature > 120°C for 3 consecutive readings) and pushes immediate push notifications via WebSockets.
4. Time-Series Storage (TimescaleDB / InfluxDB): Ingests raw data using Hypertables with automatic chunk-based disk compression (90% compression ratio).
5. Continuous Downsampling: Roll up 5-second raw data into 1-minute, 1-hour, and 1-day averages after 30 days to optimize storage.
